source.title: Parameterized complexity of machine scheduling: 15 open problems

accepted.question_text: Is the single-machine scheduling problem 1||sum w_j T_j, which minimizes total weighted tardiness, fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p_max, the maximum processing time of any job?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1. Is 1||ΣwjT j fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the maximum processing time pmax?
If each job j ∈ J has a due date dj ∈ N, we also minimize – the total weighted tardiness P j∈J wjT j, where T j = max{0, dj − Cj}, and – the weighted number of tardy jobs, P j∈J wjUj.

accepted.question_text: Does the single-machine precedence-constrained scheduling problem 1|prec|sum w_j C_j admit a kernel whose size is polynomial in the gap between the optimum objective value and the lower bound given by the natural LP relaxation?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2. Does 1|prec|ΣwjCj admit a problem kernel of size polynomial in the difference between the optimum and the lower bound obtained from its natural LP relaxation?

The objective functions γ that we aim to minimize are – the makespan Cmax = max{Cj | j ∈ J}, where Cj is the completion time of job j in a schedule, and – the weighted sum of completion times, P j∈J wjCj, when each job j ∈ J also has a weight wj ∈ N.

accepted.question_text: Are the single-machine throughput problems 1|r_j|sum U_j and 1|r_j|sum w_j U_j W[1]-hard when parameterized by p_max, the maximum processing time?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3. Are 1|rj |ΣUj and 1|rj |ΣwjUj W[1]-hard parameterized by the maximum processing time pmax?
Release dates. Each job j may have a release date rj, before which it cannot be started. In this case, we add “rj” to the β-field.

If each job j ∈ J has a due date dj ∈ N, we also minimize – the total weighted tardiness P j∈J wjT j, where T j = max{0, dj − Cj}, and – the weighted number of tardy jobs, P j∈J wjUj, where Uj = 0 if job j is finished by its due date and Uj = 1 otherwise. This is equivalent to maximizing throughput—the weighted number of jobs that get finished by their due dates.

accepted.question_text: For single-machine makespan minimization with tau forbidden start and completion times, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by tau?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4. Is makespan minimization on a single machine with τ forbidden start and end times fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by τ?
The objective functions γ that we aim to minimize are – the makespan Cmax = max{Cj | j ∈ J}, where Cj is the completion time of job j in a schedule.

accepted.question_text: Consider P||C_max on parallel identical machines with high-multiplicity encoding, where there are p distinct processing times and both the processing-time values and the counts of jobs of each type are encoded in binary. Is this problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5. Is P||Cmax with high-multiplicity encoding fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number p of distinct processing times, that is, when job processing times pj and the number of jobs for each processing time are encoded in binary?

Parallel identical machines (denoted by “P” in the α-field). We are given a number m of parallel identical machines (that is, of the same speed). Each job j has to be processed by exactly one machine for a given amount pj ∈ N of time and each machine can process only one job at a time.

accepted.question_text: For the three-machine precedence-constrained scheduling problem P3|prec, p_j=1|C_max, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the width of the partial order induced by the precedence constraints?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6. Is P3|prec, pj=1|Cmax fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the width of the partial order induced by the precedence constraints?

Precedence constraints. If jobs are restricted by precedence constraints, then we add the qualifier “prec” to the β-field to indicate that jobs are only allowed to start after their predecessors are completed.
Processing time restrictions. If all jobs j have unit processing time, we add “pj = 1” to the β-field.

accepted.question_text: Are the parallel identical machine problems P|r_j, p_j=p|sum w_j U_j and P|r_j, p_j=p|sum U_j fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number of machines?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7. Are P|rj, pj=p|ΣwjUj and P|rj, pj=p|ΣUj fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number of machines?

Parallel identical machines (denoted by “P” in the α-field). We are given a number m of parallel identical machines (that is, of the same speed). Each job j has to be processed by exactly one machine for a given amount pj ∈ N of time and each machine can process only one job at a time.
Processing time restrictions. If all jobs j have unit processing time, we add “pj = 1” to the β-field. If all jobs j have an equal processing time p, we add “pj = p” to the β-field.

accepted.question_text: In the just-in-time or interval-scheduling problem P|M_j, d_j-r_j=p_j|sum w_j U_j on parallel identical machines, where each job can be processed only on an allowed subset of machines and its processing time equals the length of its release-to-due-date window, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number of machines?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8. Is P|Mj, dj−rj=pj|ΣwjUj fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number of machines?
Machine restrictions. If each job j can be processed only on a subset Mj of machines, we add “Mj” to the β-field.

Since we can interpret this problem as minimizing the total weight of jobs not meeting their due dates, where each job j has a processing time pj, a release date rj, and a due date dj such that dj−rj = pj, we denote the problem as P|dj−rj=pj|ΣwjUj.

accepted.question_text: Let p be the number of distinct processing times. Are each of the three preemptive parallel-machine problems P|pmtn,r_j|sum C_j, P|pmtn|sum U_j, and P|pmtn|sum T_j fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p?

evidence.quote: The three problems P|pmtn,rj|ΣCj, P|pmtn|ΣUj, and P|pmtn|ΣT j are all NP-hard.
Open Problem 9. Are the above problems fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number p of distinct processing times?
Preemption. Per default, we assume that jobs are not allowed to be preempted. Otherwise, we add “pmtn” to the β-field.

accepted.question_text: For two identical parallel machines with preemption, equal processing time p for every job, and objective sum w_j T_j, is the problem P2|pmtn, p_j=p|sum w_j T_j W[1]-hard when parameterized by the common processing time p?
accepted.context_brief: Preemptive tardiness hardness on two machines

evidence.quote: Open Problem 10. Is P2|pmtn, pj=p|ΣwjT j W[1]-hard parameterized by the processing time p of all jobs?
Processing time restrictions. If all jobs j have unit processing time, we add “pj = 1” to the β-field. If all jobs j have an equal processing time p, we add “pj = p” to the β-field.

accepted.question_text: For the three-machine flow-shop makespan problem F3||C_max, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p_max, the maximum processing time?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11. Is F3||Cmax fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the maximum processing time pmax?
Flow shop scheduling, denoted by “F” in the α-field: all jobs have the same set of operations with the same total order.

accepted.question_text: For the three-machine job-shop makespan problem J3||C_max, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized jointly by p_max, the maximum processing time, and n_max, the maximum number of operations in a job?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 12. Is J3||Cmax fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the maximum processing time pmax and the maximum number nmax of operations per job?
Job shop scheduling, denoted by “J” in the α-field: the operations of each job are totally ordered, yet each job may have a distinct total order on its operations.

accepted.question_text: Is there an algorithm that computes a (1+epsilon)-approximation for job-shop makespan minimization J||C_max in time f(m, epsilon) * poly(n), depending on the number of machines m and approximation parameter epsilon but only polynomially on the input size?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 13. Is there an algorithm that yields a (1 + ε)-approximation for J||Cmax in f(m, ε) · poly(n) time?
Job shop scheduling, denoted by “J” in the α-field: the operations of each job are totally ordered, yet each job may have a distinct total order on its operations.

accepted.question_text: For the open-shop problem O|p_ij=1, ST_sd,b|C_max with unit-time operations and sequence-dependent setup times between g batches, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number g of batches?
accepted.context_brief: Batch setup times in open shop

evidence.quote: Open Problem 14. Is O|pi j = 1, STsd,b|Cmax fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number g of batches?
Open shop scheduling, denoted by “O” in the α-field: the processing order of the operations of each job is unrestricted and must be decided by an algorithm.

Batch setup times. When jobs are partitioned into batches and a sequence-dependent setup time spq is needed when switching from a job of batch p to a job of batch q, then, in accordance with Allahverdi et al. (2008), we add “STsd,b” to the β-field.

accepted.question_text: For the open-shop throughput problem O|p_ij=1, r_j|sum w_j U_j with unit-time operations and release dates, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number of machines?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 15. Is O|pi j=1,rj|ΣwjUj fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number of machines?
Open shop scheduling, denoted by “O” in the α-field: the processing order of the operations of each job is unrestricted and must be decided by an algorithm.
Release dates. Each job j may have a release date rj, before which it cannot be started. In this case, we add “rj” to the β-field.
